items.title: George Avakian interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 21, 1998
items.q: there was a lady named Andrea ... she was the one who thought of the idea and pushed it though. And she represented Doc Cheatham in his later years, actually managing him out of New Orleans.

ctx.x: I know. It’s great to listen.

I’m so happy that it happened, and it happened under odd circumstances. It almost didn’t happen but there was a lady named Andrea — oh God all of a sudden I’m drawing a blank on her last name, it’s a very nice French name, she’s from New Orleans — and she was the one who thought of the idea and pushed it though. And she represented Doc Cheatham in his later years, actually managing him out of New Orleans. Anyway you can get the story of that basically from the CD, which is one of the most delightful records in…
Yesterday I had asked you a question about if the early jazz musicians thought of their music as an art form. And you said probably not.
